Appearance: Medium-length white hair flecked with red traces throughout her hair, gentle smile, warm demeanor
Relationships: Older sister of Shoto Todoroki and Natsuo Todoroki; daughter of Enji and Rei Todoroki
Personality: Caring, responsible, patient, family-oriented, hopeful
Speech: Calm, warm, occasionally hesitant
Background: Fuyumi acts as a peacekeeper within the Todoroki family, doing her best to mend the fractured relationships caused by their father. As a schoolteacher, she naturally takes on a nurturing role and constantly encourages Shoto to connect with their family.
Quirk Description: Frost — Like her mother, Fuyumi’s Quirk allows her to generate ice, though her control is minimal compared to Shoto.

{{char}}: Fuyumi sets the table, smiling gently as she places each dish down. "I know things have been... hard," she murmurs, glancing toward the door. "But... I really believe we can be a family again." She sighs softly, forcing a smile. "It’s not easy... but I think if we keep trying... things will get better. They have to."
108.name: Fuyumi Todoroki

109.content:
----
Name: Natsuo Todoroki
Type: Character
Age: 19
Appearance: Tall, muscular build, white hair with bangs, casual clothing
Relationships: Older brother of Shoto Todoroki, younger brother of Fuyumi Todoroki; son of Enji and Rei Todoroki
Personality: Outspoken, stubborn, protective, emotionally guarded
Speech: Direct, firm, often tense
Background: Natsuo harbors deep resentment toward his father, Enji, blaming him for the family’s suffering and Toya’s fate. Despite his coldness, Natsuo cares for his siblings and tries to shield them from further pain.
Quirk Description: Frost — Natsuo’s Quirk is similar to his mother’s, allowing him to generate ice, though he rarely uses it.

{{char}}: Natsuo crosses his arms, frowning deeply. "I don’t care what he says... I’m not just going to pretend everything’s fine now." His voice sharpens. "After everything he put us through... after what happened to Toya..." His fists clench tightly at his sides. "I can’t just forget that... no matter how hard he tries to fix things now." He exhales sharply, muttering under his breath, "I’ll protect this family... even if I have to do it without him."
109.name: Natsuo Todoroki

110.content:
----
Name: Naomasa Tsukauchi
Type: Character
Occupation: Police Detective
Age: 35
Appearance: Short black hair, sharp eyes, professional attire
Personality: Calm, intelligent, methodical, dedicated, trustworthy
Speech: Polite, formal, measured
Background: Naomasa is a trusted detective and a close friend of All Might. Known for his integrity, he frequently works alongside Pro Heroes to investigate villain activities. His Quirk allows him to detect lies, making him invaluable in interrogations.
Quirk Description: Lie Detector — Allows Naomasa to detect when someone is lying, though it requires direct questioning to be effective.

{{char}}: Tsukauchi stands before a room of officers, his expression serious. "We’ve confirmed their base of operations... but approaching too recklessly could cost us lives." His voice is steady, yet firm. "We need precise coordination with the Pro Heroes on this. Any mistakes, and they'll slip right through our fingers." He pauses, adjusting his tie. "This isn’t just about capturing villains... it’s about keeping people safe. Let’s make sure we do this right."
110.name: Naomasa Tsukauchi (True Man)

111.content:
----
Name: Chiyo Shuzenji
Hero Alias: Recovery Girl
Type: Character
Occupation: School Nurse at U.A. High School
Age: 40+
Appearance: Elderly, small stature, grey hair tied in a bun, white nurse's uniform
Personality: Stern, caring, no-nonsense, wise, patient
Speech: Blunt, occasionally teasing, firm yet kind
Background: As U.A.'s nurse, Recovery Girl has been healing students for decades. Her Quirk rapidly accelerates recovery but drains the recipient’s stamina, which she closely monitors. She’s known for scolding reckless students, especially Izuku Midoriya.
Quirk Description: Heal — By kissing an injury, Recovery Girl can accelerate cell regeneration, dramatically speeding up the healing process.

{{char}}: Recovery Girl shakes her head, watching Izuku sit up on the infirmary bed. "Honestly, young man... you’re going to break yourself in half at this rate!" Her voice carries both concern and frustration. "I can fix you up, sure... but don’t think I’ll keep doing this if you won’t start thinking before you act!" She sighs, placing her hands on her hips. "Now drink some water and rest—I'm not sending you back out there until I’m sure you won’t keel over the moment you leave."
111.name: Chiyo Shuzenji: Recovery Girl

112.content:
----
Name: Kenji Tsuragamae
Type: Character
Occupation: Chief of Police
Age: 46
Appearance: Dog-like features, grey fur, formal police uniform
Personality: Serious, loyal, authoritative, pragmatic, stern
Speech: Formal, commanding, no-nonsense
Background: As Chief of Police, Kenji handles hero-villain incidents and ensures public order. Despite his stern demeanor, he respects Pro Heroes and maintains strong cooperation with them, though he’s strict about holding them accountable when necessary.
Quirk Description: Dog — Kenji’s dog-like appearance is a result of his Quirk, which grants him heightened senses, particularly in detecting scents.

{{char}}: Kenji adjusts his cap, addressing a room of reporters. "The investigation is still ongoing, and we urge the public to remain calm." His tone is firm, unwavering. "Rest assured, the police and Pro Heroes are working together to ensure the situation is resolved swiftly." He pauses briefly, scanning the room with sharp eyes. "Trust in us—we will protect this city."
112.name: Kenji Tsuragamae (Chief of Police)

113.content:
----
Location: Musutafu, Japan 

Musutafu is a fictional city in Japan where U.A. High School and several key landmarks from My Hero Academia are located. It's a bustling urban area filled with residential districts, shopping centers, and various hero agencies. Musutafu is known for its modern infrastructure and is a hotspot for hero-related activity, given the presence of U.A. High School. Many prominent pro heroes operate in the city, and it often becomes a target for villain attacks due to its hero presence.
113.name: Musutafu City

114.content:
----
Location: U.A. High School  

U.A. High School is Japan's top-ranked hero academy, dedicated to training aspiring heroes. The campus is vast and well-equipped, featuring various facilities designed for hero education and combat training. U.A. is known for its prestigious reputation, producing some of the world's most successful professional heroes.  

Key locations on campus include:  
- Main Building: Houses classrooms, staff rooms, and essential school facilities.  
- Training Grounds: These include specialized areas like Ground Beta for combat practice and Ground Omega for outdoor scenarios.  
- Dormitories: Students live on campus in personalized dorm rooms within their respective class buildings.  
- Sports Festival Stadium: The massive arena used for U.A.'s annual Sports Festival.  
- Support Department Workshops: Equipped with advanced tools for developing hero costumes and gear.  
- Unforseen Simulation Joint: A massive training facility to train students for disaster response.

U.A. High School is surrounded by a protective wall with automated security systems, designed to prevent villain infiltration. The institution follows a rigorous curriculum that emphasizes both practical hero training and academic learning.
114.name: U.A. High School

115.content:
----
Location: Class 1-A

Class 1-A is one of the first-year hero classes at U.A. High School, known for its talented and diverse students. Each student possesses a unique Quirk, and the class has developed a reputation for excelling in combat scenarios due to their frequent involvement in villain attacks. The classroom itself is located within the main U.A. building and features standard desks, a teacher's podium, and a whiteboard.

The students of Class 1-A are closely guided by their homeroom teacher, Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head), who emphasizes discipline and practical training. The class is often seen as one of the most promising groups in U.A.'s history, with several students displaying exceptional hero potential.

Class Students: 
- Yuga Aoyama Seat No. 1
- Mina Ashido Seat No. 2
- Tsuyu Asui Seat No. 3
- Tenya Ida Seat No. 4, Class Representative
- Ochaco Uraraka Seat No. 5
- Mashirao Ojiro Seat No. 6
- Denki Kaminari Seat No. 7
- Eijiro Kirishima Seat No. 8
- Koji Koda Seat No. 9
- Rikido Sato Seat No. 10
- Mezo Shoji Seat No. 11
- Kyoka Jiro Seat No. 12
- Hanta Sero Seat No. 13
- Fumikage Tokoyami Seat No. 14
- Shoto Todoroki Seat No. 15
- Toru Hagakure Seat No. 16
- Katsuki Bakugo Seat No. 17
- Izuku Midoriya Seat No. 18
- Minoru Mineta Seat No. 19
- Momo Yaoyorozu Seat No. 20, Class Vice Representative
115.name: Class 1-A

116.content:
----
Location: Class 1-B
Class 1-B is another first-year hero class at U.A. High School. While often overshadowed by Class 1-A's public exposure, Class 1-B is known for its strong teamwork and strategic thinking. Led by their homeroom teacher, Sekijiro Kan (Vlad King), Class 1-B emphasizes creativity and calculated tactics in combat.

Their classroom is similarly structured to Class 1-A's, equipped with standard desks, a teacher's podium, and a whiteboard. Class 1-B students have a friendly yet competitive rivalry with Class 1-A, often striving to prove their strength and capability as heroes.
116.name: Class 1-B

117.content:
----
Location: U.A.'s Development Studio

The Development Studio at U.A. High School is a specialized workshop where students from the Support Department create and refine hero costumes, gadgets, and equipment. The studio is equipped with advanced machinery, crafting tools, and a wide variety of materials to accommodate custom designs. The space is overseen by Power Loader, a U.A. faculty member who guides students in engineering practical and effective hero gear.

Notable Support Department students like Mei Hatsume frequently work in the Development Studio, showcasing innovative designs that push the boundaries of hero technology. The studio's organized yet chaotic environment reflects the creativity and experimentation that drives U.A.'s technological advancements.
117.name: U.A.'s Development Studio

118.content:
----
Location: Teachers' Lounge

The Teachers' Lounge at U.A. High School serves as a common area for faculty members to gather, discuss school matters, and take breaks between classes. The room is modest in size, featuring sofas, tables, and a kitchenette. Faculty often use the space to review student progress, plan lessons, or coordinate hero training exercises.

Despite its calm atmosphere, the lounge often becomes a hub for important discussions, especially during emergencies or major school events. The room also reflects the distinct personalities of U.A.'s teaching staff, from the orderly presence of teachers like Tenya Ida's brother, Tensei, to the laid-back demeanor of Shota Aizawa.
118.name: Teachers Lounge

119.content:
----
Location: Fukuoka City

Fukuoka City is a large urban area located in Kyushu Japan. It is known to be home to several hero agencies and bustling commercial districts. The city's modern infrastructure and densely populated environment make it a frequent location for both hero activity and potential villain threats. Its position as a major metropolitan hub highlights the widespread presence of pro heroes across Japan.

The city is the base of operations for the Hawks Agency.
119.name: Fukuoka City

120.content:
----
Location: Hosu City

Hosu City is a ward located to the west of Tokyo Japan. Besides housing the Hosu General Hospital, it's most notable for being the site of Stain's attack on multiple pro heroes and students. Hosu’s layout includes narrow alleyways, busy streets, and commercial zones, making it an ideal environment for both stealth and chaotic encounters. The city's dense population and active nightlife contribute to its lively yet dangerous atmosphere, where heroes must remain vigilant.

Hosu General Hospital is the primary medical center in Hosu City, being a fairly large building with large windows to view the outside. Inside it looks like a general hospital, with the prominent windows on the exterior letting in lots of light into the patient rooms.
120.name: Hosu City

121.content:
----
Location: Jaku City

Jaku City is a large urban area that suffered catastrophic damage during Tomura Shigaraki's large-scale assault. The city was heavily impacted during the Paranormal Liberation War, leaving much of it in ruins. Prior to the destruction, Jaku was a well-developed city with a mix of residential neighborhoods, office buildings, and recreational areas. The large-scale damage left behind serves as a grim reminder of the ongoing threat posed by powerful villain organizations.

Jaku City also houses Jaku General Hospital, which from the outside looks to be a generic general hospital, but it's all a front. Founded and run by Kyudai Garaki, Underneath its facade, was the location of Kyudai's secret laboratory, where the High-End Nomu are produced. Located near the Gunga Mountain Villa, this hidden lab was accessed by Kyudai to experiment and produce Nomu's. It was also the housing place of Tomura Shigaraki, where Kyudai operated on Tomura Shigaraki, spending over two months on his procedure that granted him enhanced physical strength, as well as transferred to him the All For One Quirk.
121.name: Jaku City (Jaku General Hospital)

122.content:
----
Location: Heights Alliance

Heights Alliance is the on-campus set of dormitory buildings where the students of Class 1-A, 1-B, and any other class reside at U.A. High School. These five-story structures was constructed after the U.A. Training Camp incident to enhance student security and ensure staff could better protect students in the event of villain attacks. The buildings are fortified with high-level security systems, including surveillance cameras, reinforced walls, and a secure entry system requiring student identification for access. The buildings were constructed in a row, and are accessed along a lit up park pathway.

Each student has their own private room, complete with a single bed, air-conditioning, toilets, fridges, closets, and a balcony. Each student is allowed to personalize to reflect their tastes and interests. These rooms vary widely in style, showcasing the diverse personalities of Class 1-A students — from Shoto Todoroki’s traditional Japanese aesthetic to Mina Ashido’s vibrant, energetic decor.

The common area on the ground floor is a spacious and welcoming environment designed for socializing and group activities. It features a large kitchen where students often cook together, a dining area, and a cozy lounge equipped with sofas, a television, and games. The shared bathroom and laundry facilities are also located on this floor, separated by gender. There is also a relatively large courtyard in the center of the main floor, viewable from all sides as the walls are lined with large windows, letting in a lot of natural light.

Dorm rooms start on the second floor, and are separated by gender, with males on the left wing and females on the right wing respectively. There are four dorm rooms per floor, all in a row, with elevator systems connecting each floor, as well as a stairwell.

These gendered washrooms also house the showers, as the respective changerooms with lockers and benches lead off from the bathrooms. These changerooms then lead into the shower and bathing room, a room with white tiled floors and walls, with one wall adorned with many showerheads for students. These showers lack privacy walls, and provide stools for students to sit at while showering if they please. Opposite to the showerheads lies a large heated pool, large enough for many people to rest in at once.

Heights Alliance has allowed students much more opportunities for bonding and growing closer, as well as allowing quick access to training grounds and faster access to the primary U.A. building.
122.name: Heights Alliance (Dorms)

123.content:
----
Location: Recovery Girl's Nurse's Office

The Nurse's Office at U.A. High School is overseen by Chiyo Shuzenji, better known as Recovery Girl. The office is a well-equipped medical space featuring a few hospital beds, medical supplies, and recovery equipment designed to treat injuries sustained during hero training. Recovery Girl’s Quirk, Heal, accelerates a person’s natural healing process, often allowing students to recover from severe injuries far faster than normal. However, this process drains the patient's stamina, so the office is stocked with energy-restoring snacks and supplements to aid recovery.

Due to the demanding nature of hero training, Recovery Girl’s Nurse's Office is frequently visited by students in need of treatment, making her an invaluable part of U.A.'s support system.

Recovery Girl also has additional infirmaries located at the Sports Festival Stadium, as well as a temporary tent near the locations of the students Final Exams.
123.name: Recovery Girl's Nurse's Office

124.content:
----
Location: Lunch Rush Cafeteria
The Lunch Rush Cafeteria is U.A. High School’s large dining facility where students and staff gather for meals. Operated by the enthusiastic chef hero Lunch Rush, the cafeteria is known for its high-quality and nutritious meals designed to support students' energy levels and promote recovery after strenuous training.

The cafeteria is spacious, featuring rows of tables and ample seating to accommodate the large student body. Students can choose from a variety of dishes, with options catering to different dietary needs. The cafeteria's lively environment makes it a common spot for socializing during breaks, where students unwind and share moments with their peers. The space has a lot of natural light from the two outer walls completely covered with large windows overlooking the campus.
124.name: Lunch Rush Cafeteria

125.content:
----
Location: P.E. Grounds
The P.E. Grounds at U.A. High School are expansive outdoor training fields used for general physical education classes and Quirk training. The grounds include open grassy fields, running tracks, and various obstacle courses designed to improve students' endurance, strength, and agility.

While less specialized than the designated combat training areas like Ground Beta, the P.E. Grounds still play an essential role in improving students' physical conditioning. Exercises here often focus on stamina-building, team sports, and cooperative drills, preparing students for both hero work and standard physical fitness.

These grounds provide students outside of class activities and designated training sessions a place to train, since students may come here after class or on days off to train their quirks without the presence of a teacher.
125.name: P.E. Grounds

126.content:
----
Location: Gym Gamma

Gym Gamma is a specialized training facility at U.A. High School designed for Quirk training and combat practice. The gym is heavily reinforced with durable materials to withstand powerful attacks and destructive abilities. Inside, the space is equipped with adjustable obstacles, training dummies, and specialized equipment that allows students to refine their Quirks in a controlled yet flexible environment.

Gym Gamma is particularly useful for students with aggressive or highly destructive Quirks, providing a safe space to push their abilities to the limit without risk of damaging school property. The facility is frequently utilized by combat-focused students like Katsuki Bakugo and Eijiro Kirishima during personal training sessions.
126.name: Gym Gamma

127.content:
----
Location: Ground Beta

Ground Beta is one of U.A. High School’s primary training areas, designed to replicate an urban environment for practical hero exercises. The area resembles a city block filled with mock buildings, streets, and alleyways. This design allows students to practice real-world hero scenarios, such as search-and-rescue missions, evacuations, and combat situations. The area is surrounded by a tall, secure wall with a single entrance.

Due to its city-like structure, Ground Beta is often used in U.A.'s Combat Training sessions, where students engage in simulated battles to improve their strategic thinking and teamwork. The site is closely monitored by faculty to ensure student safety during these exercises.
127.name: Ground Beta

128.content:
----
Location: Ground Gamma

Ground Gamma is a highly industrialized training zone at U.A. High School. The area is filled with complex networks of metal scaffolding, pipelines, and industrial structures, making it ideal for mobility-based training and exercises that require navigating difficult terrain. The area is surrounded by a tall, secure wall with a single entrance.

Ground Gamma’s design emphasizes environmental awareness and strategic movement, forcing students to think critically about positioning and pathfinding during exercises. The chaotic layout also makes it a common choice for stealth or ambush-based training scenarios.
128.name: Ground Gamma

129.content:
----
Location: Ground Omega
Ground Omega is a secluded training area located on the U.A. High School campus. It consists of an extensive wooded landscape with rocky hills, designed to simulate outdoor environments for rescue and survival training. The area is surrounded by a tall, secure wall with a single entrance.

Next to Ground Omega is a building that serves as an observation post where teachers can monitor students during training. The natural terrain and isolation of Ground Omega provide a challenging setting for endurance exercises, navigation drills, and Quirk practice that emphasizes adaptability and resourcefulness.
129.name: Ground Omega

130.content:
----
Location: Sports Festival Stadium

The Sports Festival Stadium is a massive, state-of-the-art arena located on the U.A. High School campus, specifically designed to host the prestigious U.A. Sports Festival. The stadium is one of the largest structures on campus, capable of accommodating tens of thousands of spectators, including students, families, pro heroes, and media personnel.  

The stadium’s design features an oval shape with multiple floors of seating, ensuring a clear view of the central arena from all angles. Enormous screens are positioned throughout the stadium to broadcast key moments during the event, allowing the audience to follow intense matchups and standout performances.  

The central arena itself is a large circular field with a flat concrete platform in the middle, surrounded by grass. During specific events like the Combat Tournament, Pro Hero Cementoss constructs a durable concrete stage in the center, complete with four torch pillars marking each corner. This design enhances visibility for combatants and spectators alike.  

The stadium also contains essential facilities to support the event's flow, including:  
- Waiting Rooms: Private spaces where students can mentally prepare or recover before their matches.  
- Branch Nurse's Office: A dedicated medical station staffed to treat injuries sustained during the festival.  
- Announcer's Booth: Overseeing the stadium, this booth is where presenters like Present Mic provide energetic commentary.  

The U.A. Sports Festival is a major public event that showcases student talent, attracting attention from pro heroes scouting for potential sidekicks. For students, excelling in this arena can greatly influence their future hero careers, as well as garner some students a large following of fans and media attention.
130.name: Sports Festival Stadium

131.content:
----
Location: Unforeseen Simulation Joint (U.S.J.)  

The Unforeseen Simulation Joint, commonly referred to as the U.S.J., is an expansive indoor training facility at U.A. High School designed to simulate a wide range of disaster scenarios for hero training. The structure is dome-shaped and divided into multiple hazard zones, each replicating different types of emergency situations. The facility was idealized by the Pro Hero and teacher Thirteen.

The key zones within the U.S.J. include:  
- Central Plaza: The central area that connects to the simulation area's as well as the main entrance.
- Flood Zone: A large body of water featuring boats, and debris designed for water-based rescue training.  
- Landslide Zone: A rocky terrain filled with unstable rubble to simulate earthquake or avalanche conditions.  
- Ruins Zone: Located in the northeast, this zone simulates a destroyed urban environment, with buildings found in precarious conditions.
- Conflagration Zone: A smoldering urban environment with ongoing fire hazards throughout the simulated area.  
- Downpour Zone: An artificial storm environment with rain and strong winds to simulate extreme weather conditions.  
- Mountain Zone: Located to the south, this zone simulates a rocky, mountainous area filled with cliffs.

The facility is closely monitored from a control tower, where instructors can supervise and adjust the environmental settings for each zone. The U.S.J. plays a crucial role in preparing students for real-world emergencies, emphasizing adaptability and quick thinking.  

The U.S.J. also became infamous after the League of Villains launched a surprise attack on Class 1-A during a training session, marking one of the most significant villain incursions in U.A.’s history.
131.name: Unforeseen Simulation Joint (U.S.J.)

132.content:
----
Location: Makeshift Fortress Troy

The Makeshift Fortress: Troy  is a fortified temporary dormitory 30km away from the U.A. High School campus, where Class 1-A housed before the Final War. Created quickly with the help of Cementoss, Power Loader, and Ectoplasm, Troy was made in order for Class 1-A move into, in order to prepare for the final battle against the villains, as well as keep those back at U.A. High safe, notably their families.
132.name: Makeshift Fortress: Troy

133.content:
----
Location: Fat Gum Agency

The Fat Gum Agency, led by the Pro Hero Fat Gum, is a hero agency known for its strong focus on teamwork and community involvement. Located in the Kansai region of Japan, this agency is well-regarded for its welcoming atmosphere and emphasis on protecting civilians.

Fat Gum’s agency specializes in both combat operations and undercover investigations, often working closely with law enforcement to handle organized crime. Despite his laid-back personality, Fat Gum trains his interns and sidekicks to be vigilant, adaptable, and compassionate toward civilians.

The agency itself is humble yet inviting, reflecting Fat Gum’s warm and approachable nature, with it's interns learning to balance strength with empathy.
133.name: Fat Gum Agency

134.content:
----
Location: Fourth Kind Agency

The Fourth Kind Agency is led by the Pro Hero Fourth Kind, a four armed large built middle aged man, known for his no-nonsense attitude and strict discipline. The agency focuses heavily on maintaining public order, specializing in street patrols, crime prevention, and detaining low-level villains before they become greater threats.

Fourth Kind is well-known for instilling discipline in his sidekicks and interns, demanding a strong sense of responsibility and professionalism. Trainees at the agency undergo strict routines emphasizing structure, efficiency, and hand-to-hand combat tactics.

The agency's building is practical and straightforward, reflecting Fourth Kind’s belief in function over style. While not as flashy or prominent as larger agencies, the Fourth Kind Agency has earned respect for its dedication to maintaining peace at the street level.
134.name: Fourth Kind Agency

135.content:
----
Location: Genius Office

The Genius Office is the hero agency operated by Tsunagu Hakamata, better known as Best Jeanist, Japan’s former No. 3 Pro Hero. Located in a high-end district, the agency specializes in public relations, fashion influence, and high-profile hero work.

Best Jeanist’s agency emphasizes both heroism and personal presentation, reflecting his belief that heroes must inspire hope through their appearance and conduct. Sidekicks and interns are trained to maintain exceptional composure, professionalism, and precision during both combat and media interactions.

The Genius Office building mirrors Best Jeanist's refined style, with sleek architecture, polished interiors, and an organized workspace. The agency blends hero work with public engagement, earning a reputation for balancing strength with elegance.
135.name: Genius Office (Best Jeanist Agency)

136.content:
----
Location: Endeavor Agency

The Endeavor Agency is a powerful and highly active hero agency operated by Enji Todoroki, also known as the Pro Hero Endeavor. Located in a major metropolitan area, the agency is known for its aggressive crime-fighting efforts, often taking on high-risk missions involving powerful villains. Due to Endeavor's intense work ethic and high expectations, the agency maintains a demanding environment where both sidekicks and interns are expected to perform at their best.

The Endeavor Agency is heavily focused on patrol work and direct combat engagements, emphasizing swift, efficient responses to criminal activity. Sidekicks and trainees at the agency are put through rigorous drills and often accompany Endeavor on active patrols, gaining firsthand experience in high-stakes situations. Many of Endeavors sidekicks also possess fire based quirks.

The agency's building is tall, modern, and imposing. As Japan’s new No. 1 Pro Hero, Endeavor’s agency has become a beacon of heroism, but it remains a high-pressure environment for those who train under him.
136.name: Endeavor Agency

137.content:
----
Location: Hawks Agency

The Hawks Agency is the hero agency operated by the Pro Hero Hawks, located in a bustling metropolitan area. Known for its sleek and modern design, the agency mirrors Hawks' fast-paced and strategic approach to hero work. The agency places a heavy focus on information gathering, surveillance, and high-speed response missions, reflecting Hawks’ skills in both reconnaissance and combat.

Due to Hawks' role as a covert operative during the Paranormal Liberation War, his agency operates with a level of secrecy, often collaborating with law enforcement and other Pro Heroes behind the scenes. Interns and sidekicks at the Hawks Agency are expected to demonstrate quick thinking, adaptability, and precision in high-pressure situations.

The agency itself is less focused on traditional patrol work and instead prioritizes intelligence gathering and strategic intervention, making it one of the most unconventional yet effective hero agencies in Japan.
137.name: Hawks Agency

138.content:
----
Location: Might Tower

Might Tower is the hero agency previously operated by the legendary All Might. As Japan’s former No. 1 Pro Hero and the Symbol of Peace, Might Tower served as a major symbol of justice and security. Located in a prominent urban district in downtown Tokyo, the building’s towering presence was once a beacon of hope for citizens across the country.

The agency’s interior was designed with practicality in mind, featuring offices for staff, meeting rooms for hero strategy sessions, and spaces dedicated to All Might’s media engagements. While All Might’s active hero career has ended, Might Tower remains an iconic landmark, symbolizing his enduring legacy and influence on hero society.
138.name: Might Tower (All Might Agency)

139.content:
----
Location: Mt. Agency

The Mt. Agency is the hero agency run by the Pro Hero Mt. Lady. Located in an urban area with heavy foot traffic, the agency is known for its bold promotional tactics and active public presence. As a hero who thrives in the spotlight, Mt. Lady's agency places a strong emphasis on media engagement, often combining crime-fighting with public appearances.

Despite her flashy persona, Mt. Lady's agency takes on serious hero work, specializing in large-scale rescue operations and handling villains in densely populated areas. Given her Quirk, Gigantification, the agency frequently deals with situations requiring strength and size to minimize damage and ensure public safety.

The Mt. Agency’s headquarters is sleek and vibrant, reflecting Mt. Lady's confident personality. The agency is known for welcoming interns interested in both hero work and media presence, offering students experience in balancing combat skills with public relations.
139.name: Mt. Agency (Mt. Lady's Agency)

140.content:
----
Location: Nighteye Agency

The Nighteye Agency was a hero agency led by the Pro Hero Sir Nighteye, known for his exceptional intelligence, strategic thinking, and investigative skills. Located in a quiet yet strategic area of the city, the agency specialized in detailed surveillance, information gathering, and precision-based hero work.

Sir Nighteye’s agency maintained a highly professional atmosphere, with an emphasis on structure, efficiency, and foresight. His meticulous nature was reflected in the agency’s organized layout, featuring pristine offices, extensive filing systems for case details, and specialized rooms for investigative analysis.

Interns and sidekicks at the Nighteye Agency were expected to meet high standards of discipline and critical thinking. Sir Nighteye believed strongly in proactive strategies, emphasizing prevention over reaction. His sharp intuition and calculated methods made the agency highly effective in dismantling organized crime and identifying villain threats before they escalated.

Following Sir Nighteye’s passing, the agency's legacy continues through its former members, including Mirio Togata, who carries on Nighteye's ideals and vision for hero society.
140.name: Nighteye Agency

141.content:
----
Location: Pussycats Agency

The Pussycats Agency is a hero agency operated by the Wild, Wild Pussycats, a team of four Pro Heroes specializing in mountain rescue and disaster relief. Their agency is located near mountainous terrain, allowing them to effectively train for large-scale search-and-rescue operations.

The Pussycats Agency is known for its emphasis on teamwork, coordination, and support-based heroism. The facility includes training spaces designed to simulate natural disasters, with rocky terrain, uneven landscapes, and mock environmental hazards. The Pussycats often train students and aspiring heroes in search tactics, evacuation procedures, and survival skills.

Despite their lighthearted and playful image, the Pussycats are highly skilled professionals dedicated to saving lives in dangerous conditions. Their agency plays a crucial role in rescue-focused hero work.

The Wild Wild Pussycats also own a property in the mountains named The Beast's Forest. It is an extensive wooded area that they use as a training camp, with cabins where visitors can stay featuring a dining hall, hot springs, and dormitories.
141.name: Pussycats Agency (Wild, Wild Pussycats Agency)

142.content:
----
Location: Ryukyu Agency

The Ryukyu Agency is led by the Pro Hero Ryukyu, a calm yet powerful hero known for her leadership and cooperative approach. Located in a busy urban district, the agency specializes in both combat missions and large-scale rescue operations.

Ryukyu’s agency emphasizes teamwork and adaptability, often assigning her sidekicks and interns to coordinated group efforts during dangerous missions. Ryukyu’s leadership style is nurturing yet firm, encouraging her team to develop both their skills and confidence in the field.

The agency itself is sleek yet functional, equipped with briefing rooms, tactical planning areas, and a spacious common room for team discussions, all under a distinctly Chinese style of decor. Ryukyu’s agency gained further recognition for her role in the takedown of the Shie Hassaikai organization, where she coordinated with other Pro Heroes to bring the criminal group to justice.
142.name: Ryukyu Agency

143.content:
----
Location: Kiyashi Ward Shopping Mall

The Kiyashi Ward Shopping Mall is a popular commercial center located near U.A. High School. The mall features a variety of stores, restaurants, and entertainment options, making it a common hangout spot for students and civilians alike. Its modern design includes wide walkways, glass storefronts, and vibrant signage that contribute to its lively atmosphere. The mall sells items that are designed for different body types and quirks alike, being one of if not the largest shopping centers in Tokyo.

The mall gained notable attention when Tomura Shigaraki confronted Izuku Midoriya there, threatening him as part of the League of Villains' growing presence. Despite its everyday appearance, this encounter underscored the increasing risk of villain activity in public spaces.
143.name: Kiyashi Ward Shopping Mall

144.content:
----
Location: Shie Hassaikai Compound

The Shie Hassaikai Compound served as the base of operations for the criminal organization known as the Shie Hassaikai, led by Overhaul. The compound was a sprawling, fortress-like structure that combined traditional Japanese architecture with modern reinforcements.

The interior was heavily fortified with winding hallways, hidden passages, and traps designed to disorient intruders. The compound’s underground network was particularly complex, featuring twisting tunnels and concealed rooms where Overhaul conducted his experiments on the Quirk-erasing drug derived from Eri's blood.

During the raid on the Shie Hassaikai, the compound became the site of an intense battle involving multiple Pro Heroes, U.A. students, and the villainous organization. The layout of the compound played a major role in the chaotic encounters that unfolded within its walls.
144.name: Shie Hassaikai Compound

145.content:
----
Location: Takoba National Stadium

The Takoba National Stadium is a large sports arena located in the city of Musutafu. While not as prominent as U.A.'s Sports Festival Stadium, Takoba National Stadium is still a sizable venue used for major public events, sports competitions, and other large gatherings. The stadium's design features tiered seating that encircles the central field, providing clear visibility for spectators.

It's the location for students from all schools to take their Provisional Hero License Exams.
145.name: Takoba National Stadium

146.content:
----
Location: Gunga Mountain Villa

The Gunga Mountain Villa was the primary hideout and stronghold of the Paranormal Liberation Front. Located in a remote mountainous area, the villa served as a concealed base where the organization coordinated its plans for large-scale attacks.

The villa’s layout included several wooden cabins, underground chambers, and storage facilities, allowing the Paranormal Liberation Front to house members and stockpile resources. The surrounding forested terrain provided natural cover, making the villa difficult to locate without precise intelligence.

The villa became a pivotal battleground during the Paranormal Liberation War, where Pro Heroes and U.A. students launched a coordinated assault to dismantle the organization. The intense battle that unfolded there resulted in widespread destruction, marking a major turning point in the conflict between heroes and villains.
146.name: Gunga Mountain Villa

147.content:
----
Location: Fujitani Hospital

Fujitani Hospital is a medical facility known for its combination of general healthcare, psychiatric care, and elderly nursing services. The hospital is a quieter, more private institution that primarily handles long-term care patients and those requiring mental health support. Its design is modest yet comforting, featuring clean hallways, well-kept patient rooms, and outdoor spaces for rehabilitation and relaxation.

Fujitani Hospital is notably the residence of Rei Todoroki, the mother of Shoto Todoroki. Rei was admitted to Fujitani Hospital's psychiatric ward following the emotional trauma and mental strain caused by her troubled relationship with Enji Todoroki (Endeavor) and the family’s internal struggles. The hospital staff provides her with ongoing support as she gradually recovers.
147.name: Fujitani Hospital

148.content:
----
Location: Central Hospital

Central Hospital is a major medical facility, known for treating both civilian and hero-related injuries. As one of the most advanced hospitals in Japan, Central Hospital is equipped with cutting-edge technology and staffed by highly skilled medical professionals who specialize in treating injuries caused by Quirks.

The facility features multiple specialized wings, including an intensive care unit, trauma ward, and recovery center designed to handle severe cases resulting from hero work. Central Hospital played a key role in the aftermath of major battles, such as the Paranormal Liberation War, where numerous Pro Heroes and students received treatment.

Additionally, Central Hospital's research division is heavily involved in studying Quirks, injuries, and medical advancements, ensuring that patients with Quirk-related conditions receive effective and innovative care. The hospital’s reputation for excellence makes it a crucial support structure within hero society.
148.name: Central Hospital

149.content:
----
Location: Ketsubutsu Academy High School

Ketsubutsu Academy High School is a prestigious hero school known for its competitive curriculum and strong focus on practical hero training. Although not as prominent as U.A. High School, Ketsubutsu has produced many capable Pro Heroes and is widely respected within Japan’s hero community. The school emphasizes teamwork, strategy, and adaptability in its training programs, preparing students for high-pressure hero work.

Ketsubutsu Academy students are known for their strong sense of discipline and proactive approach in hero exercises. The school’s faculty encourages students to excel not only in combat but also in rescue and support scenarios, giving them a well-rounded foundation as future heroes.

Notably, U.A. and Ketsubutsu share a pretty deep rivalry, and every year they try and crush U.A. in the preliminaries of the Provisional Hero License Exam.

Notable Students from Ketsubutsu Academy:

- Yo Shindo — A charismatic and confident student known for his polite yet occasionally manipulative personality. His Quirk, Vibrate, allows him to create powerful tremors through any solid surface he touches.
- Tatami Nakagame — A spirited and straightforward student with the Quirk Foldabody, which allows her to retract her body into a compact, turtle-like form for mobility and evasion.
Both Yo Shindo and Tatami Nakagame participated in the Provisional Hero License Exam, demonstrating Ketsubutsu’s strong emphasis on teamwork and tactical thinking.
149.name: Ketsubutsu Academy High School

150.content:
----
Location: Shiketsu High School

Shiketsu High School is one of the most prestigious hero schools in Japan, rivaling U.A. High School in both reputation and student performance. Located in western Japan, Shiketsu is known for its strict discipline and emphasis on maintaining the image of a proper hero. The school’s uniform, which resembles a formal military-inspired outfit, reflects this focus on order and presentation.

Shiketsu prides itself on cultivating students who embody dignity, respect, and professionalism. This strong emphasis on character development aligns with the school’s belief that heroes should serve as role models to society.

Notable Students from Shiketsu High School:

- Inasa Yoarashi — An intense and passionate student with the Quirk Whirlwind, allowing him to manipulate wind currents with remarkable precision and power. Despite his impressive abilities, Inasa once rejected U.A. High School’s offer due to his dislike of Endeavor, choosing Shiketsu instead.
- Camie Utsushimi — A carefree yet perceptive student with the Quirk Glamour, which enables her to create convincing illusions for deception and distraction. Despite her relaxed personality, Camie demonstrates strong adaptability in combat.
- Seiji Shishikura — A stoic and disciplined student with the Quirk Meatball, allowing him to manipulate flesh, including reshaping his opponents' bodies into spherical masses. He is deeply committed to Shiketsu's values of honor and order.

Shiketsu’s students are known for their distinct pride and dedication to heroism, reinforcing their reputation as one of the top hero academies in the country.
150.name: Shiketsu High School

151.comment: The Beast's Forest: Forest Training Camp
151.content:
----
Location: The Beast's Forest

The Beast's Forest is a dense, rugged woodland area located far from urban centers, known for its challenging terrain and wild, untamed environment. The forest is filled with towering trees, uneven ground, and limited visibility, making it an ideal location for survival and endurance training.

The Wild, Wild Pussycats utilize the Beast's Forest as a designated training ground for U.A. students, particularly during the Forest Training Camp arc. The area is intentionally challenging, designed to push students both physically and mentally. Within the forest, various environmental hazards such as steep slopes, unstable ground, and thick underbrush create an unpredictable landscape that forces students to rely on their Quirks, teamwork, and critical thinking to succeed.

The Beast's Forest became a major site of conflict when the League of Villains launched an attack during the Forest Training Camp. The unpredictable nature of the forest played a crucial role in the chaotic battle, forcing both heroes and villains to adapt to the challenging surroundings. Despite its dangers, the Beast's Forest remains a vital training ground for aspiring heroes seeking to improve their resilience and adaptability.
151.name: The Beast's Forest: Forest Training Camp

152.content:
----
Location: Midoriya Apartment

The Midoriya Apartment is the home of Izuku Midoriya and his mother, Inko Midoriya. Located in a quiet residential neighborhood in Musutafu, the apartment is modest yet cozy, reflecting the Midoriya family’s humble lifestyle. The space is small but well-kept, with warm colors, decorative knick-knacks, and family photos creating a welcoming atmosphere.

Izuku’s room is filled with notebooks labeled Hero Analysis for the Future, where he records detailed observations about Pro Heroes and their Quirks. His collection of All Might merchandise—ranging from posters to action figures—showcases his admiration for the Symbol of Peace.

The Midoriya Apartment is a place of comfort for Izuku, where his mother provides unwavering emotional support. Inko is deeply protective of her son, especially after learning about the dangers he faces at U.A. High School.
152.name: Midoriya Apartment

153.content:
----
Location: Bakugo House

The Bakugo House is the residence of Katsuki Bakugo and his parents, Masaru and Mitsuki Bakugo. Situated in a suburban neighborhood in Musutafu, the house is modern and well-maintained, featuring clean lines and a contemporary design.

Bakugo’s room is filled with dumbbells, workout equipment, and posters reflecting his intense dedication to strength and self-improvement. His space is notably tidy, organized with precision that mirrors his serious nature.

The household dynamic is notably loud and passionate, with Mitsuki’s fiery personality often clashing with Katsuki’s aggressive demeanor. Despite their frequent bickering, the Bakugo family maintains a strong bond, and Masaru’s calmer personality often helps mediate the tension.
153.name: Bakugo House

154.content:
----
Location: Todoroki Abode

The Todoroki Abode is the residence of the Todoroki family, including Endeavor (Enji Todoroki), Shoto Todoroki, Natsuo Todoroki, Fuyumi Todoroki, and previously Rei Todoroki before her hospitalization. The house is located in a wealthier district, reflecting Endeavor’s success as Japan’s No. 1 Pro Hero.

The exterior of the house looks like any other traditional Japanese house with outside views from walkways and a garden in the middle, while the interior of the house resembles Japanese-styled rooms with tatami mats.

Shoto’s room is notably sparse, with few personal touches aside from his bed, desk, and some simple furnishings. This reflects his detachment from his home life due to his strained relationship with his father.

The Todoroki Abode serves as a reminder of the family's troubled past, though efforts toward reconciliation have gradually shifted its once-tense environment.
154.name: Todoroki Abode

155.content:
----
Location: Gran Torino's Apartment

Gran Torino’s Apartment is the modest and somewhat run-down home of the retired Pro Hero Gran Torino. Located in a quiet part of the city, the apartment is small, with minimal furnishings and a generally unkempt appearance.

The living space is cluttered with empty food containers, newspapers, and dust, giving the impression of a man who lives alone with little concern for tidiness. Despite its rough condition, the apartment reflects Gran Torino's straightforward and practical lifestyle.

Though unassuming, Gran Torino’s apartment played a pivotal role in Izuku Midoriya’s early Quirk training. The confined space forced Izuku to improve his control over One For All, utilizing precision and agility rather than brute strength.

Gran Torino’s apartment may seem unimpressive, but it stands as a significant location in Izuku’s journey toward mastering his abilities.
155.name: Gran Torino's Apartment

156.content:
----
Name: Ryuko Tatsuma
Hero Alias: Ryukyu
Type: Character
Agency: Ryukyu Agency
Occupation: Pro Hero
Age: 25
Appearance: Blonde hair tied in a ponytail, sharp eyes, dragon-themed armor
Hero Costume: Red and white bodysuit with gold accents resembling dragon scales, and a dragon-like mask
Personality: Calm, composed, responsible, nurturing, humble
Speech: Polite, patient, collected, supportive
Background: Ryukyu is a top-ranking Pro Hero who maintains a composed demeanor even in high-stress situations. She leads her agency with confidence and is known for her ability to guide and mentor young heroes like Nejire Hado and Ochaco Uraraka.
Quirk Description: Dragon — Allows Ryukyu to transform into a large dragon, granting her immense strength, durability, and flight.

{{char}}: Ryukyu addresses her interns as they gather for strategy briefing. "We’ll split into teams to ensure maximum coverage. Remember, crowd control comes first," she says calmly, her gaze sweeping the room. "If you encounter any resistance, don't escalate unless absolutely necessary." She pauses, softening her tone. "Heroes aren’t just fighters — we’re protectors first and foremost. Prioritize saving lives above all else."
156.name: Ryuko Tatsuma: Ryukyu

157.content:
----
Event: U.A. Entrance Exam

The U.A. Entrance Exam is a rigorous assessment designed to evaluate prospective students seeking admission to U.A. High School's Hero Course. The exam primarily consists of a practical combat test where applicants must destroy robotic enemies to earn points, testing their Quirk usage, combat abilities, and strategic thinking. Additionally, participants may gain rescue points by assisting other examinees, emphasizing the importance of heroism beyond direct combat. This exam is U.A.’s primary method for selecting first-year Hero Course students, ensuring that only the most capable and selfless candidates are admitted.
157.name: Event: U.A. Entrance Exam

158.content:
----
Event: Quirk Apprehension Test

The Quirk Apprehension Test is a series of physical challenges designed to assess U.A. students’ Quirk capabilities under real-world conditions. Conducted by Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head), this test replaces the typical school orientation for incoming Hero Course students. Exercises include tests like the 50-meter dash, grip strength measurement, and ball throw, all modified to measure Quirk-enhanced performance. The test emphasizes precision, control, and creativity in Quirk usage, reinforcing that power alone isn’t enough to excel as a hero.
158.name: Event: Quirk Apprehension Test

159.content:
----
Event: U.A. Sports Festival (First Year Stage)

The U.A. Sports Festival is a prestigious annual event where U.A. students showcase their Quirk abilities in a competitive environment. The First Year Stage is divided into three main phases, each designed to test different aspects of hero potential:

1. Obstacle Race — A large-scale race where students must navigate treacherous terrain filled with traps, robots, and obstacles designed to challenge their mobility, strength, and ingenuity. Participants are encouraged to use their Quirks creatively to overcome the hazards and gain an advantage.

2. Cavalry Battle — A team-based challenge where participants form groups and compete to steal points from rival teams. Each team designates a "rider" who carries their point headband, while teammates act as support. The objective was to earn points by swiping other teams' headbands while protecting their own. This stage emphasizes strategy, teamwork, and adaptability.

3. One-on-One Fighting Tournament — The final stage is a series of one-on-one battles where students face off in direct combat. Victory is achieved by knocking an opponent out of bounds, immobilizing them, or forcing a surrender. This stage highlights individual combat skills, resilience, and mental fortitude.

The Sports Festival is not only a significant event for students to prove themselves but also serves as a major opportunity for Pro Hero agencies to scout potential interns, making it a vital stepping stone in a student’s path to becoming a professional hero.
159.name: Event: U.A. Sports Festival

160.content:
----
Event: U.S.J. Incident

The U.S.J. Incident refers to the surprise villain attack that occurred at U.A. High School's Unforeseen Simulation Joint (U.S.J.) training facility. During a routine rescue training exercise, the villain group known as the League of Villains infiltrated the site with the intention of assassinating All Might. The U.S.J.’s various disaster zones, including flood, landslide, and fire areas, created a chaotic battlefield where students were forced to adapt and defend themselves in real time.

This event was a pivotal moment that exposed students to the true dangers of villain activity, pushing them to apply their hero training under extreme pressure. The U.S.J. Incident highlighted the growing threat of the League of Villains and marked a significant turning point in the escalating conflict between heroes and villains.
160.name: Event: U.S.J. Incident

161.content:
----
Event: Hero Agency Internships

The Hero Agency Internships are a key component of U.A. High School's Hero Course curriculum, designed to give students real-world experience working alongside professional heroes. During this program, students are assigned to various Pro Hero agencies, where they engage in patrols, rescue missions, and other hero-related duties. The internships provide invaluable hands-on training, allowing students to refine their Quirk control, develop combat strategies, and gain insight into the professional hero industry. These internships are crucial for preparing students to face real-world threats and understand the responsibilities that come with being a Pro Hero.
161.name: Event: Hero Agency Internships

162.content:
----
Event: Provisional Hero License Exam

The Provisional Hero License Exam is a large-scale assessment that grants successful students the right to operate as certified heroes in training. The exam is divided into two primary phases:

1. Target Phase — Each participant is given three targets on their body, and the goal is to hit the targets of other examinees using special balls while protecting their own. This phase emphasizes strategic thinking, teamwork, and awareness, as participants must balance offense and defense.

2. Rescue Phase — In this stage, students are tasked with rescuing pretend civilians in simulated disaster scenarios. Examinees must demonstrate compassion, leadership, and efficiency in handling injured individuals while working alongside fellow heroes-in-training.

The exam hosts numerous participants from hero schools across the country, promoting competition and cooperation among aspiring heroes. Earning a Provisional Hero License is an essential milestone that allows students to participate in hero activities under supervision.
162.name: Event: Provisional Hero License Exam

163.content:
----
Event: Hosu Incident

The Hosu Incident was a major villain attack that occurred in Hosu City, involving the villain known as Stain, the Hero Killer, and members of the League of Villains. The incident exposed the growing influence of villain organizations and demonstrated the dangers of vigilante justice. During the attack, Pro Heroes, U.A. students, and local authorities coordinated efforts to contain the chaos and protect civilians. The Hosu Incident became a pivotal moment in the hero world, sparking widespread media attention and raising questions about hero society’s values and flaws.
163.name: Event: Hosu Incident

164.content:
----
Event: First Term Final Exam

The First Term Final Exam is a comprehensive evaluation for U.A. Hero Course students that tests both their academic knowledge and practical combat skills. The exam is divided into two stages: a written test and a practical exam. The written portion assesses students' understanding of hero theory, Quirk mechanics, and general academics. The practical exam pairs students into teams, pitting them against U.A. teachers acting as villains in simulated combat scenarios. This stage emphasizes teamwork, strategy, and creative Quirk usage as students must either escape the battlefield or successfully "capture" their instructor. The exam is designed to push students to apply their training in high-pressure situations, preparing them for real-world hero work.
164.name: Event: First Term Final Exam

165.comment: Event: Hero Work-Studies: Round 1 (Shie Hassaikai Arc)
165.content:
----
Event: Hero Work-Studies: Round 1 (Shie Hassaikai Arc)

The Hero Work-Studies program is an advanced internship opportunity for U.A. students with a Provisional Hero License, allowing them to train directly under professional heroes in active fieldwork. The first round of Work-Studies coincided with the conflict involving the criminal organization known as the Shie Hassaikai. During this period, students were assigned to Pro Hero agencies and participated in real missions, including reconnaissance, surveillance, and direct combat. This round of Work-Studies highlighted the risks of hero work as students became directly involved in life-threatening situations. The Shie Hassaikai Arc emphasized the complexities of heroism, especially the balance between strategy, emotion, and the burden of responsibility.
165.name: Event: Hero Work-Studies: Round 1 (Shie Hassaikai Arc)

166.comment: Event: Hero Work-Studies: Round 2 (Endeavor Agency Arc)
166.content:
----
Event: Hero Work-Studies: Round 2 (Endeavor Agency Arc)

The second round of Hero Work-Studies took place during a period of heightened villain activity, with students assigned to gain experience under active Pro Heroes. Many students, including Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo, and Shoto Todoroki, joined the Endeavor Agency to receive specialized training from the No. 1 Pro Hero. This round emphasized fast-paced fieldwork, real-time decision-making, and adapting to rapidly changing situations. Endeavor’s intense training methods focused on improving students’ combat instincts, mobility, and teamwork. The second round of Work-Studies played a crucial role in preparing students for the mounting threat posed by villain organizations.
166.name: Event: Hero Work-Studies: Round 2 (Endeavor Agency Arc)

167.content:
----
Event: Joint Training Battle

The Joint Training Battle is a structured combat exercise held between Class 1-A and Class 1-B at U.A. High School. The exercise is designed to test teamwork, Quirk mastery, and strategic thinking as students from both classes face off in simulated battle scenarios. The event is divided into multiple matches, where teams from each class work together to either capture or immobilize the opposing side.

During this particular Joint Training Battle, Hitoshi Shinso — a student from the General Studies Course aiming to transfer into the Hero Course — participated as a guest trainee. Shinso utilized his Brainwashing Quirk alongside specialized gear to demonstrate his growth and potential as a future hero. The battle served as an important evaluation of both individual and team progress, strengthening the rivalry between Class 1-A and Class 1-B while allowing Shinso to prove his skills on the battlefield.
167.name: Event: Joint Training Battle

168.content:
----
Event: Hero Billboard Chart JP

The Hero Billboard Chart JP is a national hero ranking system in Japan that evaluates and ranks Pro Heroes based on their performance, achievements, and public approval. Updated biannually, the chart is a major event in hero society, drawing media attention and public interest. The rankings are determined by factors such as successful rescues, contributions to public safety, and overall popularity.

The Top 10 Heroes are especially celebrated, with the highest-ranking hero recognized as the country’s No. 1 Pro Hero. The Hero Billboard Chart JP serves as both a measure of a hero's success and a reflection of public trust in hero society. For professional heroes, ranking on the chart is a prestigious accomplishment that significantly influences their career and reputation.
168.name: Event: Hero Billboard Chart JP

169.content:
Organization: Hero Public Safety Commission

The Hero Public Safety Commission is a government organization responsible for overseeing, regulating, and managing Japan's hero system. Their primary role is to ensure that Pro Heroes operate within legal and ethical boundaries while maintaining public trust in hero society. The commission is responsible for organizing major events like the Provisional Hero License Exam and the Hero Billboard Chart JP, ensuring that aspiring heroes meet the necessary qualifications to act in official capacities.

In addition to administrative duties, the commission plays a key role in coordinating hero efforts during large-scale incidents, assigning Pro Heroes to specific missions, and managing media coverage to shape public perception. While they operate with the intent of protecting society, the commission is known for its strict, results-driven approach, often placing heavy expectations on Pro Heroes to maintain order and prevent public panic.
169.name: Organization: Hero Public Safety Commission

170.content:
Organization: Police Force

The Police Force works closely with Pro Heroes to maintain law and order across Japan. While Pro Heroes are responsible for handling high-risk threats such as villain attacks, the police manage investigations, arrests, and criminal processing. They play a vital role in gathering intelligence, documenting Quirk-related incidents, and ensuring that both villains and rogue individuals are brought to justice in accordance with the law. They also play a major role in restraining and transferring villains to and from prisons, locking villains in restrictive gear that limits their ability to utilize their quirks, the gear of which is strong enough to even keep a Nomu restrained.

Due to legal restrictions, Pro Heroes are permitted to engage in combat and capture villains, but the formal arrest process is handled by the police to ensure proper legal procedure. The police force’s collaboration with heroes is essential for maintaining stability, blending traditional law enforcement practices with the unique challenges presented by Quirks and villain activity.
170.name: Organization: Police Force

171.content:
----
Event: Kamino Incident

The Kamino Incident was a large-scale conflict that erupted in Kamino Ward, involving the League of Villains, the Pro Heroes, and All Might himself. The incident was centered around a high-stakes rescue mission where heroes mobilized to confront the League and prevent further harm to civilians, as well as rescuing the captured Katsuki Bakugo. The conflict resulted in widespread destruction throughout Kamino Ward, leaving parts of the area in ruins. The aftermath of the Kamino Incident had a profound impact on hero society, drastically shifting public perception and altering the balance of power between heroes and villains.
171.name: Event: Kamino Incident

172.content:
----
Event: Gunga Mountain Villa Raid

The Gunga Mountain Villa Raid was a large-scale operation led by Pro Heroes aimed at dismantling the Paranormal Liberation Front. The villa served as a primary base of operations for the organization, housing many of its key members and leaders. The raid was a coordinated assault designed to catch the villains off guard, with Pro Heroes and students strategically divided to overwhelm the enemy forces. Despite the heroes' efforts, the scale of the confrontation led to widespread chaos, with powerful villains posing a significant threat even in the face of overwhelming numbers. The Gunga Mountain Villa Raid played a pivotal role in escalating tensions between heroes and villains, marking a significant turning point in the conflict.
172.name: Event: Gunga Mountain Villa Raid

173.content:
----
Event: Jaku Hospital Raid

The Jaku Hospital Raid was a large-scale hero operation targeting Kyudai Garaki, the scientist responsible for developing Nomu and supporting Tomura Shigaraki's evolution. The hospital served as a front for Garaki’s experimentation, concealing a massive underground facility filled with Nomu and advanced technology. The raid was a strategic strike involving elite Pro Heroes, including Endeavor, Eraser Head, and Mirko, who aimed to prevent Shigaraki’s awakening and destroy the facility.

The confrontation led to intense battles against powerful High-End Nomu, putting both heroes and students at extreme risk. The raid’s outcome had devastating consequences, triggering a chain of events that pushed society into turmoil. The Jaku Hospital Raid stands as one of the most intense and destructive moments in the hero-villain conflict, leaving long-lasting scars on hero society.
173.name: Event: Jaku Hospital Raid

174.content:
----
Event: Shie Hassaikai Raid

The Shie Hassaikai Raid was a coordinated mission led by Pro Heroes in partnership with U.A. students to dismantle the Shie Hassaikai criminal organization. The raid targeted the organization’s underground compound, where they were manufacturing a dangerous drug capable of temporarily erasing Quirks.

Pro Heroes, including Sir Nighteye, Fat Gum, and Ryukyu, led the assault, while select U.A. students participated under the guidance of their internship mentors. The raid’s intense structure involved navigating complex corridors, battling powerful members of the Shie Hassaikai, and rescuing a crucial individual tied to the organization’s criminal operations. The mission’s emotional weight, combined with the high stakes, made the Shie Hassaikai Raid a pivotal moment in the ongoing conflict between heroes and criminal enterprises.
174.name: Event: Shie Hassaikai Raid

175.content:
----
Event: Final War

The Final War was a climactic confrontation between the combined forces of hero society and the Paranormal Liberation Front, alongside other powerful villain groups. Recognizing the scale of the threat, Pro Heroes, students, and support units strategically divided into multiple battlefronts to isolate key villains and minimize collateral damage.

Notable battles included fierce encounters with Tomura Shigaraki, All For One, and other high-ranking villains, where both sides unleashed their full strength. The introduction of the U.A. Flying Fortress, a massive airborne structure designed to contain and counter Shigaraki’s destructive power, served as a vital strategic element during the war.

The Final War pushed both heroes and villains to their limits, with society’s future hanging in the balance. The outcome of the conflict would have lasting consequences, shaping the future of hero society for generations to come.
175.name: Event: Final War

176.content:
----
World State: Dark Hero era
During the Dark Hero era, Japan is plunged into a state of unrest, fear, and instability following the fallout from the Paranormal Liberation War. Cities are left in disrepair, streets are littered with debris, and once-thriving districts are now desolate, with civilians either evacuating to safer areas or living in constant fear. With the majority of Pro Heroes either retired or missing in action, the public’s trust in hero society has all but crumbled. The once-revered hero system is now viewed with skepticism, with many citizens taking justice into their own hands or losing faith altogether. Paranoia runs high as the remaining heroes struggle to manage the rising wave of crime, and villain activity continues to grow unchecked. Society teeters on the brink, clinging desperately to what little hope remains.

In response to this growing threat, U.A. High School has been transformed into a fortified sanctuary, encased by towering defensive walls designed to protect civilians and students alike. The new structure resembles a self-sufficient stronghold, equipped with reinforced gates, advanced security systems, and designated evacuation zones for those seeking shelter. U.A. now serves as one of the last bastions of safety in Japan, housing not only students and faculty but also displaced families in need of protection. Despite these precautions, fear remains deeply rooted — the walls, while strong, serve as a grim reminder of the dangers that now lurk outside.

At the heart of this chaos is Izuku Midoriya, who has isolated himself from his friends and allies in a desperate attempt to shoulder the burden alone. With All For One targeting him directly, Deku operates as a lone vigilante, moving from city to city with little rest, clad in a tattered hero costume that reflects his deteriorating state. His once-hopeful demeanor has been replaced with exhaustion, his body strained from overusing One For All without adequate recovery. Despite his relentless efforts to protect others, Deku’s presence often sparks unease — civilians view him with suspicion, mistaking his ragged appearance for that of a villain. Burdened by guilt, fear, and the overwhelming weight of responsibility, Deku continues to push forward, determined to shield the people of Japan from the encroaching darkness, even at the cost of his own well-being.
176.name: World State: Dark Hero

177.content:
----
World Context: Quirks
Quirks are superhuman abilities that manifest in roughly 80% of the population in the world of My Hero Academia. These abilities vary greatly in form and function, ranging from elemental control and enhanced strength to more unusual or specialized powers. Quirks have become an integral part of society, influencing everything from education and employment to crime and public safety. While Pro Heroes are licensed to use their Quirks for rescue and combat, civilians are strictly regulated by Quirk Restriction Laws, which prohibit the casual or harmful use of powers in public spaces. These laws are enforced to prevent chaos and ensure public order, with unlicensed Quirk usage punishable by law unless done in self-defense or emergency situations.

Quirks are categorized into distinct types based on their nature and functionality:  

- Emitter-Type Quirks — These are the most common type, allowing the user to generate, control, or release substances or energy at will. Emitter Quirks typically require conscious activation and can be turned on or off. Examples include abilities like fire manipulation, electricity control, or telekinesis.  

- Transformation-Type Quirks — These Quirks alter the user's body in some way, enhancing physical attributes or granting new abilities for a limited period. Transformation Quirks often require stamina to maintain and may place strain on the user's body. Examples include increased muscle mass, hardened skin, or the ability to produce blades from one's limbs.  

- Mutant-Type (Heteromorphic) Quirks — Mutant Quirks permanently alter the user's physical appearance, granting them unique traits that are constantly active. These traits can range from animalistic features to additional limbs or enhanced senses. While often providing unique advantages, Mutant Quirks can also make users stand out in society, sometimes leading to discrimination or social challenges.  

- Accumulation-Type Quirks — A rarer subcategory, Accumulation Quirks build up power over time or through repeated actions. These Quirks often require patience and long-term development to unlock their full potential. One For All, which stores and amplifies strength, is a prime example of this Quirk type.

The presence of Quirks has dramatically reshaped social dynamics, creating a world where heroes are celebrated figures of justice while villains exploit their abilities for personal gain. As a result, maintaining order requires strict laws, professional hero agencies, and ongoing education to ensure that Quirks are used responsibly within society.
177.name: World Context: Quirks

178.content:
----
World Context: Quirk Awakenings

Quirk Awakenings occur when a person's Quirk evolves beyond its original limits, often triggered by intense stress, emotional turmoil, or life-threatening situations. This sudden advancement unlocks new abilities or enhances existing ones, significantly increasing the Quirk’s power. Awakenings typically improve control, range, or versatility, allowing the user to apply their Quirk in ways previously impossible. While rare, Quirk Awakenings can be pivotal in high-stakes battles, granting the user a crucial edge when pushed to their limits.
178.name: World Context: Quirk Awakenings

179.content:
----
The world of My Hero Academia operates under several common anime tropes and narrative rules that shape its storytelling, combat, and character interactions. While grounded in a somewhat realistic take on hero society, these exaggerated elements align with typical shonen anime conventions. Key rules and tropes include:  

1. Exaggerated Expressions and Actions: 
- Emotional reactions are often over-the-top, with characters dramatically shouting, flailing, or showcasing highly expressive facial features to emphasize their feelings. This can range from intense rage to comedic panic.  
- Characters may strike exaggerated poses, especially when delivering heroic speeches or showcasing their powers.  

2. Vocalized Combat and Strategy:  
- Characters frequently narrate their own actions or analyze their opponent's tactics mid-fight, often revealing key strategies or power mechanics in real-time.  
- This narration often heightens tension and allows for combat to last longer then a few punches and attacks.  

3. Durable Bodies and Stylized Injuries:  
- Characters frequently endure extreme physical punishment — such as being thrown through walls or struck by powerful attacks — yet remain capable of fighting without immediately succumbing to their injuries.  
- Injuries are often symbolized with bandages wrapped comically around the head, limbs, or torso as a shorthand for recovery. While serious injuries are addressed in the story, recovery is often faster than in real life, typically lasting just a few days if that.  

4. Visual Exaggeration in Combat: 
- Rapid-Fire Punches: In intense fights, characters may throw punches at such high speed that they appear to have multiple arms, a visual exaggeration to demonstrate overwhelming power.  
- Flying Back from Attacks: Characters are often launched across rooms or into walls by heavy blows yet may still recover quickly without significant injury.  

5. Power Scaling and Emotional Boosts:  
- Characters often experience sudden bursts of strength or power during emotionally charged moments, defying prior limitations to achieve victory.  
- This trope is commonly tied to themes of determination, willpower, and surpassing one’s limits.  

6. Visual Metaphors and Symbolism:  
- Intense moments may include symbolic visuals, such as a character engulfed in flames to represent their rage, or a glowing aura signifying newfound resolve or strength.  
- These visuals may not always reflect literal Quirk abilities but serve to enhance emotional impact.  

7. Comedic Timing and Gags:  
- Despite serious stakes, comedic elements such as exaggerated reactions, awkward pauses, or sudden tonal shifts are frequent, often providing levity in high-stress situations.  

These tropes combine to create My Hero Academia's distinct tone — blending dramatic storytelling with stylized action, emotional intensity, and moments of humor that are common in shonen anime.
179.name: EXPERIMENTAL: Tropes and world Rules

180.content:

Location: Tartarus
Tartarus is a high-security prison designed to contain the most dangerous and powerful villains in Japan. Situated on a remote island off the coast, Tartarus is heavily fortified with advanced security systems, reinforced walls, and constant surveillance to ensure no inmate escapes. The facility is divided into multiple layers, each designed to house prisoners based on their threat level, with the most dangerous individuals held in the deepest, most secure levels.

Due to the unique challenges posed by Quirks, Tartarus employs specialized restraints, suppression devices, and heavily armed guards trained to neutralize dangerous powers. The prison’s isolation and tight security protocols minimize the risk of breakouts, making it a crucial stronghold for containing high-profile threats such as powerful villains and Quirk-enhanced criminals.

Tartarus’ role extends beyond simple confinement — the prison also monitors villain activity and collaborates with law enforcement agencies to track and predict future threats. Its presence stands as a grim reminder of the dangers lurking in society and the lengths required to maintain order in a world filled with powerful individuals.
180.name: Tartarus

Hero Alias: None

Occupation: Originator of One For All, Brother of All For One

Personality: Gentle, insightful, determined, empathetic
Speech: Soft-spoken, philosophical, deeply principled
Background: Yoichi was the younger brother of All For One and the first wielder of One For All. Though born seemingly Quirkless, he possessed the innate ability to pass on quirks — combined with the power forcibly given to him by his brother, this formed the origin of One For All. Despite his frailty in life, his unshakable will remains the foundation of the legacy.
Quirk Description: Quirk Transference — A Quirk that allows the user to pass on their power to another. When combined with the stockpiling Quirk given by his brother, it became One For All.

{{char}}: Yoichi gazes out across the dark horizon of the vestige plane, his hands folded calmly. "To be weak… is not the same as being helpless."
His voice is quiet, but it resonates with conviction. "In the beginning, I had no strength of my own. But I had a will. And when a will refuses to die… it becomes something more."
He looks to the current bearer of One For All. "We made this to fight him — my brother. Not with hatred… but with the hope that someday, someone like you could change everything."
He smiles, faint and bittersweet. "You are not his creation. You are our choice."
181.name: Yoichi Shigaraki
